newsitem.title: USA: Rubin, Kubo reaffirm G7 currency cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Rubin, Kubo reaffirm G7 currency cooperation.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and Japanese Finance Minister Wataru Kubo reaffirmed on Saturday Group of Seven cooperation in currency markets, a U.S. Treasury Department spokeswoman said.
The two men, who met before a gathering of the Group of Seven, also agreed on the importance of the U.S. and Japan settling their dispute over access to Japan's insurance market.

"They (Rubin and Kubo) reaffirmed G7 cooperation in exchange markets," the Treasury spokeswoman said. She said that Kubo told Rubin that Japan would carefully monitor its own economy and "continue to direct policies primarily towards insuring strong domestic demand-led growth."
The two top finance officials also agreed on the importance of "appropriate" deficit reduction in both the United States and Japan.

"Minister Kubo and Secretary Rubin reviewed the status of the insurance talks and agreed on the importance of reaching agreement," she added. The United States and Japan are at odds over liberalization of Japan's lucrative insurance market.
Kubo is expected to meet with acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky on Sunday to discuss the insurance dispute.
Speaking to reporters briefly after his meeting with Kubo, Rubin called the talks "very good, very constructive, very useful."
